title: C.D. Jackson released the Zapruder film with frames missing

tellings.quote: the guy who led out the Zapruder film is a guy named Charles Douglas Jackson
Life acquired the Zapruder film, the clearest footage of the assassination, but instead of releasing it in full, they only published black and white stills with certain key frames missing.
tellings.difference: Adds that only black and white stills were published rather than the full film, and runs the withholding into the 1970s.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell of Life magazine under C.D. Jackson putting out the Zapruder film with key frames missing.

as_told.title: Life magazine withholds the Zapruder film under C.D. Jackson

plain: The Zapruder film is a home movie that captured the killing of President John F. Kennedy in 1963. A researcher named Jeremy Riss says the man who put it out through Life magazine was Charles Douglas Jackson, and that it was released with frames missing. Riss tells it as part of a larger case that powerful people shaped what the public saw about Kennedy's death.
